issues.detail: The Greek 'ανηγαγον αυτον' (anēgagon auton) uses the masculine pronoun 'αυτον' (him/it), referring back to 'οτε' (the Passover lamb, implied by context or the preceding sentence). The Vietnamese 'đem Ngài' (brought Him) uses a respectful pronoun 'Ngài' which usually refers to God or Jesus. In this specific context of the Law of Moses, it refers to the sacrificial lamb.

The Greek 'κατα τον νομον' (kata ton nomon) means 'according to the law'. The Vietnamese 'theo luật' is an acceptable rendering, but the phrase 'đã được trọn' (were completed/fulfilled) for 'επλησθησαν' (were fulfilled/completed) is generally acceptable.
